subject: System Design
title: Leader Election
description: A micro-lesson that makes Leader Election usable.

hook.text: Three servers all think they're the leader. Each accepts conflicting writes. Data is now corrupt.

buildup.text: Leader election ensures exactly one node is the leader at any time. It coordinates all writes.

discovery.text: Algorithms use terms or epochs — monotonically increasing numbers — to prevent stale leaders from acting.

twist.text: A split brain occurs when the network partitions and both sides elect a leader. Fencing tokens prevent this.

climax.text: Leader election is the foundation of consensus, replication, and coordination in distributed systems.

punchline.text: Exactly one leader, or the data diverges.

quiz.question: What is a split brain in distributed systems?
options: Two parts of a cluster each elect a leader after a partition
A server that runs out of memory
